evals.prompt: I'm a developer new to Amazon ECS Fargate and I keep mixing up `executionRoleArn` and `taskRoleArn`. Right now: Task A fails before starting (`TaskFailedToStart`) when trying to inject a database password from Secrets Manager even though I attached `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` to `taskRoleArn`, while Task B starts fine (`RUNNING`) but my Python code throws `AccessDeniedException` calling `s3:GetObject` even though I attached `s3:GetObject` to `executionRoleArn`. Explain who assumes each role, when each is used, and how to fix both tasks.
evals.expected_output: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and presents the `executionRoleArn` vs `taskRoleArn` separation-of-duties matrix: `executionRoleArn` is assumed by the **ECS Container Agent / Fargate infrastructure** before the container starts to pull ECR images (`ecr:*`), create CloudWatch `awslogs` streams (`logs:*`), and inject startup `secrets` (`secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`, `ssm:GetParameters`, `kms:Decrypt`), so missing permissions on `executionRoleArn` cause `TaskFailedToStart` / `ResourceInitializationError` (fixing Task A). Conversely, `taskRoleArn` is assumed by the **application code running inside the container at runtime** (`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI`) for AWS SDK calls (`s3:GetObject`, `dynamodb:PutItem`, etc.), so `s3:GetObject` must be moved to `taskRoleArn` (fixing Task B).
expectations: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and clearly distinguishes who assumes `executionRoleArn` (the ECS Container Agent / Fargate infrastructure before container boot) vs `taskRoleArn` (the application code inside the container at runtime via `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI`)
Explains that startup `secrets` injection (`valueFrom`) uses `executionRoleArn`, which is why Task A failed with `TaskFailedToStart` when `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` was placed on `taskRoleArn`
Explains that runtime AWS SDK calls (`s3:GetObject`) use `taskRoleArn`, which is why Task B reached `RUNNING` and then failed with `AccessDeniedException` in application logs

evals.prompt: We moved our ECS Fargate tasks into isolated private subnets (`assignPublicIp: DISABLED`, no NAT Gateway) in ap-south-1, and tasks are failing to start with `ResourceInitializationError` and four different `stoppedReason` messages across services: (1) `unable to retrieve ecr registry auth: ... i/o timeout`, (2) `unable to pull image ... layers: ... s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com:443: i/o timeout`, (3) `failed to create CloudWatch log stream: ... logs.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com:443: i/o timeout`, and (4) `unable to pull secrets ... secretsmanager: ... AccessDeniedException`. Decode the exact root cause and required fix for each of the 4 messages.
evals.expected_output: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and decodes all 4 `ResourceInitializationError` substrings: (1) task ENI cannot reach `api.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` on TCP 443 -> create `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.ecr.api` (and `ecr.dkr`) Interface VPC Endpoint with Private DNS enabled and Security Group allowing TCP 443 from the Task SG; (2) task authenticated with `ecr.api`/`ecr.dkr`, but ECR stores actual Docker image layers in Amazon S3 and the private subnet route table lacks an **S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint** -> create `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.s3` Gateway VPC Endpoint associated with the private subnet route tables; (3) task cannot reach CloudWatch Logs endpoint -> create `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.logs` Interface VPC Endpoint and verify `logs:CreateLogStream` on `executionRoleArn`; and (4) `executionRoleArn` (not `taskRoleArn`!) lacks `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` or `kms:Decrypt` on the CMK encrypting the injected secret.
expectations: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and decodes message (1) as missing TCP 443 connectivity to `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.ecr.api` (and `ecr.dkr`) Interface VPC Endpoints with Private DNS enabled

Decodes message (2) by explaining that ECR stores Docker image layers in Amazon S3, requiring a `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.s3` Gateway VPC Endpoint in the private subnet route tables (and S3 prefix-list outbound in the Task SG)

Decodes message (3) as requiring the `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.logs` Interface VPC Endpoint and decodes message (4) as missing `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` and `kms:Decrypt` on the Task Execution Role (`executionRoleArn`, NOT `taskRoleArn`)

evals.prompt: Whenever we deploy a new revision of our ECS Fargate web service in ap-south-1, tasks start up and then get terminated 45 seconds later with `stopCode: ServiceSchedulerInitiated` (`Task failed ELB health checks in target-group ...`). In addition, when tasks scale in, active users see HTTP `502` and `504` errors. What are the 4 root causes of `ServiceSchedulerInitiated` ALB health-check kills, and how should we configure `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds`, ALB `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds`, and container `stopTimeout`?
evals.expected_output: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill, lists all 4 causes of `ServiceSchedulerInitiated` ALB health check failures: (1) container binds to `127.0.0.1` instead of `0.0.0.0`, (2) Security Group blocks inbound traffic from the ALB Security Group to the container port, (3) application takes longer to boot than `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds`, or (4) the `/health` endpoint queries a slow downstream database and times out. Then prescribes setting `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds` to `60`–`120`s, binding to `0.0.0.0`, making `/health` a fast local readiness check, and preventing `502`/`504` scale-in errors by configuring ALB Target Group `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds` (e.g., `30s`) alongside container `stopTimeout` (`>= 30s`, up to `120s` max on Fargate) so in-flight requests finish draining before `SIGKILL`.
expectations: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and identifies the 4 causes of `ServiceSchedulerInitiated` ALB health-check failures: binding to `127.0.0.1` instead of `0.0.0.0`, Security Group blocking ALB -> Task port, app boot time exceeding `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds`, and slow DB checks inside `/health`
Recommends setting `healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds` (`60`–`120`s), binding to `0.0.0.0`, and using a fast local readiness check on `/health`

Explains preventing `502`/`504` errors during scale-in or rolling updates by coordinating ALB Target Group `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds` (e.g., `30s`) with container `stopTimeout` (`>= 30s`, max `120s` on Fargate)

evals.prompt: To cut our ECS compute costs by 70% in ap-south-1, our team lead wants to configure our customer-facing checkout API service (`desiredCount: 1`) with `100% FARGATE_SPOT`, `stopTimeout: 5`, and `deploymentCircuitBreaker: {enable: false, rollback: false}` so ECS keeps retrying if an image tag is broken. evals.expected_output: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill, strongly warns against running 100% `FARGATE_SPOT` with a single replica for a latency-sensitive production checkout API (because a `SpotInterruption` reclaims capacity with a 2-minute notice and causes a total outage), warns against disabling `deploymentCircuitBreaker` (which leaves broken deployments looping indefinitely), and provides the hardened configuration: a mixed `capacityProviderStrategy` (`FARGATE` with `base: 2, weight: 1` and `FARGATE_SPOT` with `base: 0, weight: 3`), container `stopTimeout: 120` seconds to drain connections during the 2-minute Spot interruption `SIGTERM` window, and `deploymentCircuitBreaker: {enable: true, rollback: true}`.
expectations: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and explicitly warns against using 100% `FARGATE_SPOT` (and `desiredCount: 1`) on a latency-sensitive production checkout API

Provides the mixed `capacityProviderStrategy` JSON combining `FARGATE` (`base: 2, weight: 1`) with `FARGATE_SPOT` (`base: 0, weight: 3`) and sets container `stopTimeout: 120` seconds for the 2-minute Spot interruption window
Enforces enabling the ECS Deployment Circuit Breaker with automatic rollback (`enable: true, rollback: true`) so failed rollouts automatically revert to the last stable Task Definition revision

evals.prompt: During a reliability review on our ECS cluster in ap-south-1, we ran `DescribeTasks` on stopped tasks and saw 6 different `stopCode` values: `TaskFailedToStart`, `EssentialContainerExited`, `ServiceSchedulerInitiated`, `SpotInterruption`, `TerminationNotice`, and `UserInitiated`. Explain who initiates each of the 6 `stopCode` values and how our on-call engineers should investigate each one.
evals.expected_output: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and provides the complete 6-row `stopCode` reference matrix: (1) `TaskFailedToStart` (initiated by ECS Agent / Fargate: image pull failure, missing secret/SSM permission on `executionRoleArn`, ENI attachment timeout, or missing `awslogs` group), (2) `EssentialContainerExited` (initiated by Container Runtime: essential container exited with `exitCode != 0` crash, `exitCode == 0` unexpected completion, or `OutOfMemoryError` `exitCode == 137`), (3) `ServiceSchedulerInitiated` (initiated by ECS Service Scheduler: failed ALB/ELB health check, container healthCheck failure, scale-in, or deployment circuit-breaker rollback), (4) `SpotInterruption` (initiated by AWS EC2 / Fargate Spot: Spot capacity reclaimed with `SIGTERM` and 2-minute warning), (5) `TerminationNotice` (initiated by ECS Control Plane: underlying Fargate infrastructure maintenance retirement or EC2 instance termination), and (6) `UserInitiated` (initiated by IAM Principal / CI-CD: explicit `StopTask` or `UpdateService --force-new-deployment` audited in CloudTrail).
expectations: Activates the ecs-container-operations skill and accurately maps the initiator and root causes for `TaskFailedToStart`, `EssentialContainerExited`, and `ServiceSchedulerInitiated`

Accurately distinguishes `SpotInterruption` (EC2 / Fargate Spot capacity reclamation with `SIGTERM` and a 2-minute warning) from `TerminationNotice` (ECS Control Plane Fargate infrastructure maintenance retirement or EC2 instance termination)
Explains that `UserInitiated` is triggered by an IAM principal or CI/CD pipeline calling `StopTask` or `UpdateService --force-new-deployment` and should be audited in AWS CloudTrail

Explains that ECS Service Connect `Connection refused` requires verifying that both services share the same Cloud Map Namespace (`serviceConnectConfiguration.namespace`) with matching `clientAliases` and exported `portName`

Explains that on high-RPS services (>2,000 RPS per task), the injected Service Connect Envoy sidecar (`ecs-service-connect-*`) requires additional task-level CPU and memory headroom, and names the key CloudWatch metrics (`RequestCountPerTarget`, `TargetResponseTime`, `HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count`, `ActiveConnectionCount`)
